primary_claim: Attribution-based Parameter Decomposition (APD), a new method that decomposes a network's parameters directly (rather than its activations) into minimal, faithful, simple components, is largely able to recover the ground-truth mechanisms in three toy models involving superposition and cross-layer computation, though it required heavy hyperparameter tuning and showed some mechanism mixing.
depends_on: LessWrong: BatchTopK - a simple improvement for TopK SAEs
contradicts_or_qualifies: the prior approach of decomposing network activations layer-by-layer into features and connecting them into circuits, which the authors argue may not be the way to go, citing 'Activation space interpretability may be doomed' and 'Circuits in superposition'
stated_future_work: make the method more stable, e.g. by switching attributions for trained masks optimised along with the components
make the method more computationally efficient at scale, e.g. via a two-stage rank-1 decomposition
implement APD for transformers and CNNs and test on toy models with ground-truth mechanisms
scale the method to LLMs, starting with a single-layer decomposition and comparing to SAE features
limitations_stated: results have some imperfections / some amount of mechanism mixing, suspected to be due to using top-k
too sensitive to hyperparameters to be usefully applied to larger models such as LLMs in this first prototype
quote: We find that APD is largely able to decompose these toy networks into components corresponding to individual mechanisms... However, the results required a lot of hyperparameter tuning and still exhibit some amount of mechanism mixing, which we suspect is due to our using top-k.
